name: Adrianopolis
description: A leafy upmarket district of gated towers, tree-lined avenues and the Manauara shopping mall. It holds consulates, clinics, gyms and the city's best supermarkets, and streets stay usable after dark. Most professionals and long-stay foreigners in Manaus end up renting here because the infrastructure simply works.
bestFor: Nomads who want reliable power, fast fibre and a safe walk to a mall or gym.
pros: Best-maintained apartments and fibre in the city
Malls, clinics and gyms within walking distance
Noticeably safer streets than the centre
cons: Condo-and-mall life feels sealed off from the city
Still need a car or app taxi for the river and old town

name: Ponta Negra
description: A residential and tourist strip on the Rio Negro about ten kilometres from downtown, built around a wide sandy river beach and a paved promenade of bars and kiosks. Behind it stand tall condo towers with pools. Evenings fill with joggers, live music and some of the best sunsets in Brazil.
bestFor: Nomads who want a swim, a run and a sunset beer at the end of the working day.
pros: River beach and promenade on your doorstep
Modern condos with pools and gyms
Busy bar and restaurant scene at night
cons: Long slow commute into central Manaus
Weekend crowds and loud sound systems
River level swallows the beach in the wet season

name: Vieiralves
description: Officially part of Nossa Senhora das Gracas, Vieiralves is a compact grid of restaurants, bars, cafes and small apartment blocks just north of the centre. It is where Manaus goes out for Amazonian fish, pizza and cold beer, and it stays lively on weeknights. Small enough to cover entirely on foot.
bestFor: Sociable nomads who want dinner, drinks and a cafe desk all within a few blocks.
pros: Densest cluster of restaurants and cafes in Manaus
Neighbours Adrianopolis and sits 3km from the centre
cons: Bar noise carries into apartments at weekends
Fewer large modern condos than Adrianopolis

name: Parque 10 de Novembro
tagline: Middle-class blocks around a big city park
description: A large residential district built around Parque dos Bilhares, with running tracks, food kiosks and a mix of older houses and mid-rise flats. It sits between the centre and the northern zone, so buses and app taxis reach both easily. Rents run well below Adrianopolis for similar-sized apartments.
bestFor: Nomads staying a few months who want space and a park without upmarket prices.
pros: Real park with running and exercise areas
Cheaper rent than the upscale districts nearby
Good bus links in both directions
cons: Traffic on Avenida Constantino Nery is relentless
Few cafes set up for laptop work
Housing stock is mixed and often dated

name: Centro
description: The historic core, holding the Teatro Amazonas opera house, the floating port, the Adolpho Lisboa market and streets of faded belle epoque facades. By day it is a loud open-air commercial zone of stalls and shoppers. Cheap rooms are plentiful, and the boat terminals for Amazon trips are right there.
bestFor: Short-stay nomads using Manaus as a launchpad for river trips.
pros: Walk to the opera house, markets and boat docks
Strong local food for under $5 a plate
cons: Empties out and gets risky after dark
Petty theft is common in the market streets
Noisy, humid and short on decent apartments
